# I’m Mary Ann “MJ” Jawili
I’m running for El Cerrito City Council.

## Why I’m running
I am running because El Cerrito deserves a leader who can bring its residents together, and I have a successful track record of listening with empathy, engaging people, and building community. I am running because I love El Cerrito, and I want to help it become a better, more inclusive, more sustainable, and thriving place to live. I am running because I think that public service is deeply rewarding, and I want to serve as an example to other people to show that they can do it, too.
## Contact me
I love hearing from people.
Contact me by phone or email.
votemjforec@gmail.com
(510) 467-0757
## My vision
### Better connection, communication, and transparency
I believe that trust and safety are built on connection, communication, and transparency. Politics in El Cerrito have become fraught and divisive over the past few years. Lack of transparency has caused a breakdown in trust between residents and city council. I will work to foster a city council environment that provides more opportunities to hear from residents, be responsive to input, and be transparent in the decision-making process.
#### Better city communication
I will prioritize increased communication and transparency between residents and city leadership by offering one-on-one office hours, commissioning surveys of residents, and meeting regularly with liaisons from various community groups. I also commit to communicating in plain language, across platforms and formats to meet residents’ diverse needs and preferences.
#### Build safety through trust
Everyone should feel safe calling for help—and confident that the right help will arrive. I believe public safety starts with strong relationships, prevention, dependable emergency response, and trust between residents and the people who serve them. I also believe safety and civil liberties belong together. That’s why I signed the Flock Out anti-surveillance pledge. Our community should not have to sacrifice their constitutional rights in the name of public safety. We should invest in approaches that work, measure the results, and be willing to change course when something isn’t working.
We all want to feel more connected to our neighbors and our community. Community spaces are where we run into our neighbors and build new relationships. A connected community is a safe and thriving community.
### More community spaces
#### Help local businesses thrive
I want El Cerrito to be a place where local businesses can start, stay, and grow. That means filling empty storefronts, making it easier to reuse buildings for new purposes, and helping business owners navigate City Hall without unnecessary confusion or delay. I will work to build partnerships with local businesses such as cafes, shops, and gyms to facilitate the gathering of people in the community. A thriving local economy gives us great places to gather, creates opportunities for our neighbors, and helps pay for the public services we all depend on.
#### Better and more accessible third spaces
A strong community makes room for everyone. I want children to have safe places to learn, play, and grow. I want older residents to have places to gather, activities to enjoy, transportation they can depend on, and real human beings they can turn to for help. And I want people with disabilities to be able to participate fully in community life. This means protecting and improving our community centers, parks, trails, and improving the community programs that are currently offered.
#### A multi-generational center
A community thrives when residents across age and demographics are able to interact, connect, and build relationships. Our community needs both a senior center and a better library. But given El Cerrito’s limited resources, these two needs have been pitted against each other, resulting in tensions and divisions in our community. Our seniors deserve a dependable five-day-a-week gathering place to connect with each other and get help finding the services they need. Our kids deserve a place to learn and read that is safe. I will explore options for a multi-generational center that meets all of the needs of our diverse community. Accessibility isn't an extra feature. It's part of how we build a city where everyone belongs.
### Safe transportation and mobility
We all want to be able to move through our community with ease. I aim to improve the ease and safety of transportation in El Cerrito so that it is easier for everyone to get where they want to go, connect with neighbors, and touch grass.
#### Fix our streets and stop ripping them up twice
Our streets belong to all of us, but a lot happens underneath them. Water, sewer, electricity, communications, and other infrastructure are maintained by different agencies and utilities. I want the City to coordinate those projects better so that we aren’t repaving a street only to have someone dig it up again. We should plan projects together, minimize closures and disruption, hold utilities accountable for restoring our streets properly, and make it easy for residents to know what work is happening and why.
#### Improved and diverse transportation infrastructure
I believe people should be able to easily get where they are going regardless of the mode of transportation they choose, whether that’s driving, biking, walking, or public transit. I support Complete Streets; frequent, public transit; accessible trails and sidewalks; reliable paratransit; and a functional network of transportation and mobility options for people to travel without driving themselves.
We want our community to be able to respond to and withstand anything. While we can’t predict the future, we can prepare for it with smart budgeting and disaster preparedness planning now.
### Community resilience
#### Spend our money wisely and explain where it goes
El Cerrito has worked hard to recover from serious financial problems. We need to protect that progress. I’ll push for budgets that are understandable, realistic, and focused on the services residents actually experience — from roads and parks to emergency response and recreation. When we make difficult choices, residents deserve to know why. Good financial management isn’t just about balancing the books. It’s about making sure our money delivers real value for our community.
#### Plan responsibly for pensions
We made promises to the people who worked for our city, and we need to keep them. We also need to make sure those commitments don’t crowd out the services residents depend on today. I want El Cerrito to have a clear, long-term plan for its pension obligations, with understandable public reporting and realistic assumptions about the future. Residents, employees, and retirees should all be able to understand where we stand and what we’re doing about it.
#### Prepare for the emergencies we know will come
Wildfire. Earthquakes. Extreme heat. Flooding. Power outages. Preparedness isn’t just a plan sitting on a shelf. It means knowing how we will communicate, how people will evacuate, where they can get help, and how we will support neighbors who may need extra assistance. I want El Cerrito to practice these plans, find the gaps before an emergency happens, and work closely with neighboring cities, utilities, transit agencies, and Contra Costa County.
## How I’ll lead
These policies are varied, but my approach to them is the same:
Listen first. Be honest about what we know and what we don’t. Build on what works. Learn from what hasn’t. Measure whether we’re actually making things better.
Most importantly, bring people together.
Because I don't think the challenges facing El Cerrito belong to one neighborhood, one generation, or one political camp. They're ours to solve together.

### Constituent meet-and-greet hour
Meet me every Friday from 12:00 to 1:00 PM at El Cerrito Natural Grocery & Annex. Email me at least 24 hours in advance so that I know to expect you.
If this time doesn’t work for you, request an alternate time. We’ll try to find a better time.
## Candidate statement
I've been a resident and homeowner in El Cerrito for 18 years, and I love this city. But in all the time I've lived here, I've never seen an election as polarized as our last primary. People feel they're not being listened to, and they've turned away from their city and their community as a result.
Community is what I do. From hosting dinners with friends to serving as president of an 850-member cycling club, I work to bring people together. I do this professionally, too:
For over a decade I've worked as a product leader in accessible technology, translating standards and people's needs into practical solutions that serve everyone, including people with disabilities and older adults. I've contributed to international standards and served on nonprofit boards, work that taught me how to listen, collaborate, and turn community input into tangible outcomes.
Our city deserves leadership that listens first, cares deeply, and acts with integrity. As a city councillor I'll listen with empathy, especially to residents who feel unheard. I'll proactively meet residents where they are and communicate in plain language. I'll bring transparency to how decisions are made and how money is spent. I'll keep community at the center of policy because a city's greatness is measured by how well it serves its residents.
El Cerrito doesn't need more division. It needs someone who will do the necessary work to bring us back together, and that's what I'm committed to doing.
